title: Virtual Legal & Executive Assistant — California Law Office (Remote)
description:
Virtual Legal & Executive Assistant — California Law Office (Remote)



About the Role



I'm a California attorney and real estate broker running a busy solo practice (civil litigation, landlord-tenant, probate, consumer protection) alongside several entrepreneurial ventures. I'm looking for a sharp, detail-obsessed Virtual Assistant to become my right hand — someone who takes pride in flawless work, anticipates what I need before I ask, and treats my deadlines like their own.



This is a long-term role for the right person, with growing hours and responsibility. I want someone who wants to build something with me, not someone collecting gigs.



What You'll Do



Law Office Administration (core)



Manage my calendar: court dates, filing deadlines, hearings, statute-of-limitations dates, and client meetings — with redundant reminders and zero tolerance for missed dates

Prepare and format legal documents from my drafts and templates (pleadings, discovery, correspondence, proofs of service) to California court formatting standards

Assist with e-filing in California state courts and track filing confirmations

Manage client intake: initial questionnaires, document collection, file organization, engagement letter workflows

Maintain organized digital case files with consistent naming conventions

Draft routine correspondence for my review (never sent without my approval)

Track tasks and case status across active matters; give me a weekly status digest



Executive Support



Inbox triage and
 drafting

Scheduling, travel, and vendor coordination

Light bookkeeping support (invoicing, expense tracking — no trust account access)

Research and summarize information I request (with sources)



What I'm Looking For



Meticulous by nature. You proofread everything twice. You notice when a date, name, or case number is off. In this job, small errors have big consequences.

Reliable and communicative. You hit deadlines or flag problems early — never silence, never surprises.

Discreet. You will handle confidential client information and will sign a confidentiality agreement. You understand this is non-negotiable.

A finisher. You close loops. Tasks don't sit at 90%.

Coachable and proactive. You follow my systems exactly, and you also suggest improvements when you see a better way.

Honest about AI. You may use AI tools for drafts, but you must disclose it and verify everything. Fabricated citations or unverified AI output is grounds for immediate termination.



Requirements



2+ years of experience as a VA, legal assistant, paralegal, or executive assistant (law firm experience strongly preferred)

Excellent written English

Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Word (advanced formatting), Adobe Acrobat, and task-management tools

Reliable internet, quiet workspace, and availability overlapping California business hours (minimum 4 hours/day overlap, Pacific Time)

Willingness to sign an NDA/confidentiality agreement and complete a background check



Bonus points for: California court e-filing experience, familiarity with legal calendaring rules, experience with Clio or similar practice-management software, notary or paralegal certificate.



Hours & Compensation



Starting at 20 hours/week, growing to full-time for the right person

Rate depends on experience and location — tell me your expected rate in your application

Long-term engagement; I invest in training people I keep



How to Apply



Conscientiousness starts with the application. To be considered, follow these instructions exactly:



Subject line: "Legal VA — [Your Name] — Cornerstone"

In your first paragraph, tell me about a mistake you caught before it caused a problem — yours or someone else's.

Attach your resume as a PDF named LastName_FirstName_Resume.pdf

Include your expected hourly rate and your available hours in Pacific Time.

Answer in one sentence: what does "attorney-client privilege" mean to you?



Applications that don't follow these instructions will not be read. Shortlisted candidates will complete a short paid trial task before a video interview.
